title: Look up an item with at
objective: Read one item from a list by its position, or one value from a map by its key, or one letter from a text, using at.

body.text: at reads one item. Write the name, at, then a position for a list. Positions start at 0, so the first item is at 0 and the third is at 2. A text works the same way, one letter at a time.

body.title: Positions in a list and a text
body.code:
make things equal to a list of "a", "b", "c"
say things at 0

make numbers equal to a list of 1, 2, 3
make third equal to numbers at 2
say third

make greeting equal to "hello"
make letter equal to greeting at 1
say letter

body.text: For a map, the position is a key. Write the key in quotes, or use a variable that holds a key. A list position can also be a variable.

body.title: Keys and positions in variables
body.code:
make rooms equal to a map from "entrance" to "library"
say rooms at "entrance"

make spot equal to 0
make halls equal to a list of "a", "b"
say halls at spot

body.prompt: The program prints the second item, b. Change it so it prints the third item, c.
body.starter:
make things equal to a list of "a", "b", "c"
say things at 1
body.solution:
make things equal to a list of "a", "b", "c"
say things at 2
